On this one, scrolling IS the ski run.

Powderhorn Basin is a concept build from my portfolio: a fictional cat and heli skiing operation above an invented BC town. The homepage is one mountain descended by scroll. An altimeter ticks down from the 2,610 metre drop-in while the light walks from dawn alpenglow through storm grey to valley lamplight, and by the time you reach the book button, you've already taken the run.

Under the cinema, the practical layer holds: accessibility scores of 100 on all 28 pages, and the packages page answers seats, deposits, and weather days before it asks for anything.

The operation is invented. The system is real, and it's built for any operator whose mountain deserves better than a contact form.

Take the run: powderhorn-basin.vercel.app

I built a website where you pour your own beer.

Breaker Room Brewing is a concept build: a fictional Kootenay brewery I use to show what a taproom site can feel like. Click and hold the tap, the glass fills, and every one of the eight beers pours its own way.

Nobody needs a beer-pouring website. But everybody remembers one. That's the point: in a region where most business sites look identical, feel is the difference between "seen it" and "sent it to a friend."

Pour one yourself: breaker-room-brewing.vercel.app
